title: Many hats, one message at a time
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Which hat are you wearing in this room?

A student said that Jose's brand is many-sided: involved in multiple ventures, from schools to design, and leaning on his past as a builder and teacher. Another said he is also a father and family man.

Jose said that you can have multiple brands and multiple messages, and that he tries to adapt and change hats depending on his audience. He said that he gave a talk to a group of children of very different ages and had to deliver the message in ten minutes.
He said that one of the things we can do is study the different identities we can develop.
A student said: in design there are a handful of people everyone looks up to. I follow how they gained authority. Once you build authority, you can monetize your time much better.
Jose said: you take your personality, perspective and message, and you scale it. That is what this book is about.
Which hat do you need to wear for your next audience?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the one message for each.
Write who you follow to learn how they gained authority.
Write how you could scale one message.

check.q: What did Jose say you can have?
What did Jose say he adapts to?
What did Jose say the book is about?

recap: Wear the right hat for the audience. Scale one message.
